candidate.title: OS-Seq
candidate.scope: The middle OS-Seq (oligonucleotide-selective sequencing) row of the assigned Illumina poster crop: genomic DNA fragmentation and single-adaptor addition, preparation of target-specific flow-cell primer probes, on-surface target capture and copying, bridge formation, sequencing-interface completion and paired-end readout. The depicted implementation is clarified by Myllykangas et al. (2011). The adjacent nuc-seq/SNES and Safe-SeqS rows and clipped neighboring chemistry are outside the assigned target. The independent library and surface-preparation branches converge at target hybridization; there is no depicted alternative OS-Seq workflow. Later automation, clinical panels, oligonucleotide-manufacturing subprotocols and indexing are not additional targets or expanded operations.

operations.label: Create target-specific oligos
operations.description: Introduce target-specific oligonucleotide templates and hybridize their universal region to existing flow-cell primers. The drawing under this caption shows the template/primer complex; extension of the surface primer is the next, separately captioned operation.
operations.mechanism: Complementary hybridization of the synthetic template universal region to the immobilized primer. Oligonucleotide synthesis is a preparatory source of this input, not a separately depicted synthesis workflow.
operations.information_effect: Transfers the chosen target design to a template positioned for surface-primer extension; no sample genomic sequence is measured here.

operations.label: Extend and Denature
operations.description: Extend the immobilized flow-cell primer using its annealed target-specific oligonucleotide as template, then denature that template away, leaving a surface-attached target-specific primer probe.
operations.mechanism: DNA polymerase extends the surface D primer; denaturation releases the original synthetic template. Polymerase is a catalyst, not a transferred product.
operations.information_effect: The target-recognition sequence is copied into an immobilized surface primer, linking capture specificity to the flow-cell attachment.

method_scopes.rationale: OS-Seq is the sole assigned target; oligonucleotide-selective sequencing is its expanded name. All eight local operations belong to the target row. The upper genomic-library preparation and lower surface-primer preparation are distinct branches that converge at o_capture, after which copying and bridge formation yield the sequencing interface. The three repeated Extend and Denature captions are separate local instances with different inputs and products. The primary 2011 paper supports this sequence for the depicted OS-Seq implementation; this does not assert that every later OS-Seq panel or protocol has identical complete preparation.
